Pairwise distinctness and remoteness of the selected labels and existence of their common interior point are derived from membership in the actual singleton concurrence set. Empty pointZeros gives the complete G1 condition through its already reviewed exact equivalence. In particular the proof does not require G2 at the centre, where it would be false.

The complete local crossing set is proved stable at every G1 centre. For each distinct vertex triple, nonzero determinant and continuity imply locally constant chi; repeated-index chi values are identically zero. Finiteness permits simultaneous constancy of all chi, and the actual crossing criterion transfers every unordered crossing support in both directions. This uses only G1 on the centre and nearby tuples. The criterion refers to genuine remote edge-segment intersections, so this argument covers all disjoint and transverse-interior pairs without an artificial crossing relation or a presupposed crossing inventory. The actual directed edgeParameter is the previously reviewed Cramer formula, equal to the parameter of the actual unique geometric crossing under G1. Its continuity is justified by the nonzero determinant of the actual crossing edge vectors at the centre.

The singleton concurrence produces an actual point q in the three relative interiors. G1 ensures uniqueness of each pairwise intersection and nonzero edge vectors, so the two selected parameters on any selected edge equal the parameter of q. If an additional crossing {i,h}, with h outside the selected three labels, had that same parameter, its actual crossing point would be q. The proof then places q in the interior of edge h using the genuine G1 crossing-point theorem. G1 also forces j and h to be remote because both contain q in their interiors; that remoteness is proved rather than assumed. Consequently {i,j,h} is a second actual concurrence support, and its membership in the singleton forces h into {i,j,k}, a contradiction. Thus every other central crossing parameter differs strictly from the common selected parameter.

Continuity preserves the appropriate pair of strict inequalities: every such other parameter remains smaller than both selected parameters or larger than both. Finite simultaneous intersection handles every possible partner h. The final support-equality step explicitly converts any crossing present at a nearby tuple into a crossing at the centre, so crossings absent at the centre have not been silently omitted from the neighborhood statement. The same construction is applied to the actual unordered permutations {i,j,k}, {j,i,k}, and {k,i,j}; the last permutation is proved by exact finite-set membership. All three resulting neighborhoods are intersected with complete crossing-support stability. This direct finite-neighborhood proof is a sound alternative to the source's sequence/subsequence argument and needs no sign-change hypothesis.

Adjacency is proved in the actual independently constructed Gauss list, not in an arbitrary word or a list limited to the three chosen crossings. Visit is the genuine sigma type of an actual crossing support and an incident edge. pairVisit selects the occurrence on the first specified edge, with its parameter proved equal to that actual edge's Cramer parameter. Every possible visit on that edge is exhausted by some other crossing partner. The traversal key orders first by the cyclic label's numerical representative and then by its parameter in the edge's open interval. A key strictly between two visits on the same edge therefore belongs to that same edge and has a strictly intermediate parameter. Visits whose partner is one of the two selected partners are explicitly ruled out by strict self-inequalities; all remaining partners contradict the proved outside condition. The reverse orientation is handled too. Generic on the nearby tuple supplies actual visit-key injectivity and distinct selected visits; it is provided by the punctured germ, not added to the central assumptions.

SortedAdjacency uses the true order isomorphism between the finite ordered support and Fin of its cardinality. If two member indices differed by more than one, the next index would give an actual intervening member, contradicting the gap condition. The inspected pinned Mathlib orderIsoOfFin_symm_apply identifies these indices with idxOf in the actual sorted list. gaussList remains exactly the sorted full finite universe of all visits, so neither selected element can be absent, and no intervening visits have been removed. VisitsAdjacent is the disjunction of the two genuine consecutive-index equations; its final explicit DecidableEq uses the same lifted order and has the ordinary equality meaning. Consecutive positions in this complete list imply the source's adjacency on the selected edge. Each edge's visits form one uninterrupted block, including the closing edge, so the numerical cut does not discard an edge-local endpoint case or require wraparound adjacency. The universal labelled statement is consistent with the inherited cyclic/equivariant Gauss construction.

TripleSides contains the three actual IsCrossing witnesses, all three pairwise inequalities between their actual crossingPoint values, and adjacency for the two visits on each of edges i,j,k. On edge j it uses reversed {i,j} to visit {j,i}; on edge k it uses reversed {i,k} and {j,k} to visit {k,i} and {k,j}. These are unordered-support equalities, not a reversal of polygon traversal. The three point inequalities follow from actual edge-point injectivity and the Generic/G2 parameter-distinctness theorem; the final derived Fact(1<n) only supplies the required nontrivial index instance. The aggregate therefore proves all three distinct points, not just distinct labels or two of the inequalities.

The final neighborhood result is composed with the actual continuous curve of the original WallGerm. Its intermediate condition is conditional on Generic at a nearby tuple; at every nonzero germ parameter that condition is supplied by generic_punctured. The genuine interval-subtype neighborhood is then converted to one real delta with 0<delta and delta<=g.radius using its inherited metric, whose distance from the zero parameter is abs(t). The conclusion holds for every original parameter with abs(t)<delta and t!=0, on both sides and for all three edges simultaneously. No one-sided restriction, chosen sequence, independent radius per edge, or claim of distinctness at the nongeneric centre replaces the printed punctured-neighborhood conclusion.
